tokens.{faq_q_2}: If I cannot see it, how do I know you did it?
tokens.{faq_a_2}: We verify all of our work with high-magnification inspection systems, and use machine vision and frame grabbing technologies when necessary. We supply Certificates of Conformance on request.
tokens.{faq_a_3}: Yes. We will work with you to expedite orders. On some occasions a modest fee may apply to accommodate a rush order.
tokens.{faq_q_4}: Do you accept orders for single parts and prototypes?
tokens.{faq_a_4}: Yes. We gladly accept prototyping projects and aim to build a relationship that sees your product through to production.
tokens.{faq_q_5}: In what format should drawings be submitted?
tokens.{faq_a_5}: For laser and micro-CNC projects we prefer .dxf files, with units in millimetres and the drawing centred. 3D printing projects require an .stl file; please state the unit of measure to apply.
tokens.{faq_q_6}: What is the typical lead time for a project?
tokens.{faq_a_6}: Depending on the application, some projects can be completed within 24 to 48 hours of receiving the order. More complex or higher-volume projects can take up to 2 to 3 weeks.
tokens.{faq_q_7}: What is required to get a proposal?
tokens.{faq_a_7}: Typically, a description of your project and/or a drawing.
tokens.{faq_q_8}: What is the smallest feature size that can be machined?
tokens.{faq_a_8}: About 1 micron. Feature size can be limited by the type and thickness of the material, and our staff can help you understand the limits for your material.
tokens.{faq_a_9}: Almost any material, including polymers, metals, glass and ceramics. Our relationship with Goodfellow has increased our access to new materials.
tokens.{faq_q_10}: What micro-manufacturing technologies does Goodfellow Microfabrication offer?
tokens.{faq_a_10}: A broad range, including laser machining, micro-CNC and 3D printing.
